tb21_profile.skill: Read a block-cipher's C source, implement a statistical known-plaintext key-recovery attack (linear cryptanalysis) and brute-force a reduced round-key seed space, then verify by decrypting
tb21_profile.domain: Symmetric cryptography / cryptanalysis of a Feistel cipher, C source reading, bit-level arithmetic
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec (a published attack algorithm) with an oracle-style correctness proof: decrypt all ciphertexts to a result file

searches: tools.py search rts (?i)brute[- ]?forc|crack the|recover the key|key recovery|cryptanaly|XOR
tools.py words tmax plaintext ciphertext pairs recover key round cipher attack brute-force keyspace

TMax-15K.reason: Reads a custom C++ cipher's source and recovers the secret key from intercepted plaintext-ciphertext pairs, then forges output; the FEAL crux exactly.
Literally asks for linear cryptanalysis: derive the plaintext-to-ciphertext byte relation from oracle queries, then forge a token with the recovered relation.
Write a C++ key-search that brute-forces a 16-bit residual keyspace against a known plaintext prefix and matches an oracle binary bit-exactly.
C program performing a known-plaintext attack that brute-forces a 32-bit seed, then decrypts the whole file to prove recovery.
C++ known-plaintext attack recovering a 32-bit PRNG state from a plaintext/ciphertext prefix, then bulk-decrypting; same search-and-verify loop.
Algebraic key recovery: solve for LCG seed, multiplier and increment from known plaintext, then decrypt everything - keyspace reasoning not guessing.
Recovers keystream bytes from a known magic header, then mathematically derives the unknown cipher parameters A and C; same derive-then-decrypt structure.
Brute-force a 16-bit seed from the cipher's source code and write a standalone decryptor; the reduced-keyspace hint in FEAL maps directly.
Brute-forces a 16-bit LCG seed using a known plaintext prefix and validates the candidate by SHA256 of the recovered file - same verify-by-decrypt proof.
Known-plaintext recovery of a 4-byte XOR key then batch decryption; right family but far shallower than a round-key linear attack.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Recovers a crackme's accepted password by symbolic execution rather than guessing - algorithmic key recovery against a keyspace, like the FEAL attack.
Validates an Enigma rotor configuration against a plaintext/expected-ciphertext test vector and repairs mismatches; reasoning about cipher state from pairs.
Key recovery via algorithm-confusion, then forging a valid HS256 JWT - exploit a cryptographic weakness and prove it by producing valid output.
Three crackmes where the third needs dynamic analysis; reading a binary's validation logic to derive the accepted secret.
Explicitly forbids brute-forcing: must read the check routine and deduce the password, the analytic half of a cryptanalytic attack.
Drives an Enigma M4 through encrypt and reset-and-decrypt cycles; requires correct cipher state modelling, though no key recovery.
Implement Diffie-Hellman from a written spec with an exact function contract - implement-a-crypto-algorithm-from-description, same genre as FEAL.
Reverse-engineer a crackme with objdump/gdb and verify the candidate by running the binary; analyse-then-prove loop.
Crackme trio; same reverse-engineering territory but shallow, and mostly string inspection rather than algorithmic recovery.
Another crackme-password variant; near-duplicate of rank 9 and adds nothing beyond binary inspection.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Given the cipher's source and one ciphertext, invert the custom scheme to recover the plaintext flag - a real break-the-cipher-from-its-code task.
Implements an exhaustive keyspace search over a hash; teaches writing the search loop the FEAL 20-bit-seed brute force needs.
Reverse-engineer three crackmes to derive their accepted inputs, then prove it by running them - analyse-then-verify like the FEAL decryption proof.
Recover a flag from a binary's validation check; requires reconstructing the check's arithmetic rather than guessing.
Multi-stage crypto/forensics chain (hash, key, carving) ending in a recovered flag; composite decoding pipeline but no key-recovery maths.
md5crypt hash cracking across several files with a wordlist; keyspace search in a crypto domain, but off-the-shelf tooling does the work.
Crack bcrypt hashes sharing one salt; same recover-the-secret-from-artifacts goal, but the attack is a dictionary run, not an analysis.
Emulate a binary under radare2 ESIL, reasoning about its control flow; reverse-engineering skill, no cryptography.
Stack-overflow exploitation of a CTF binary; shares the craft-an-input-that-satisfies-a-binary shape only.
Peel layered encodings off a CTF payload with a framework; decoding practice but no key recovery or algorithm implementation.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Fix AUTOSAR Profile-5 CRC and SecOC authenticator verification returning inverted results; bit-level cryptographic checking must be made exactly right.
Key-derivation produces wrong bytes and must match a literal expected key; forces reasoning about a hash-based KDF byte by byte.
CCITT G4 decoder emits wrong bit patterns; repairing it means re-deriving a bit-level coding algorithm, the same care FEAL bit masks need.
Broken LZW decoder implementation; requires reconstructing a stateful bit-stream decoding algorithm from its spec.
BER/CER/DER codec broken including indefinite-length encoding; binary-format decoding in the crypto/PKI ecosystem.
generate_uid is not uniformly or cryptographically random; the fix needs reasoning about entropy and hash output distribution.
OpenSSL cipher-list/context error handling; same crypto library ecosystem but the bug is API plumbing, not cipher maths.
struct.unpack on a short buffer must be validated; small but genuine fixed-width binary-parsing hygiene.
Native ASN.1 decoder corrupts sequence fields; field-offset reasoning over a tag-length-value binary encoding.
Big-endian byte-swap predicate is wrong; endianness reasoning transfers weakly to packing FEAL's 32-bit halves.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Buzhash XOR seed cancels itself for even windows; the fix needs algebraic reasoning about XOR rotation and a per-repo S-box, closest bit-maths here.
Encrypted-key password semantics in the main Python crypto library; same ecosystem and key-handling concepts, different work shape.
KMS sign/verify mis-encodes the digest; requires matching a signing primitive's exact byte-level contract against real cryptography output.
Binary-template interpreter mishandles implicit arrays while parsing uleb128 little-endian fields; structured binary-format reasoning.
OCSP responses built from issuer name/key hashes; PKI hashing internals in the same cryptographic ecosystem.
X509 common-name validation against RFC 5280; crypto library domain, but the work is spec-conformance checking.
KMS encryption of plaintexts over 4k; touches symmetric encryption APIs but the fix is size handling, not cryptanalysis.
Lazy variable resolution in a binary-template language; interpreter semantics with only incidental binary-parsing relevance.
KMS re_encrypt does not accept key aliases; crypto-service API plumbing with no algorithmic content.
Hidden CTF challenges answerable by brute-forcing sequential ids; security-logic bug in CTF territory, no cipher work.

final_top10.reason: Recovers a custom cipher's key from known plaintext-ciphertext pairs by reading its C++ implementation; the FEAL crux with a smaller cipher.
Explicit linear cryptanalysis: derive the plaintext-ciphertext byte relation from chosen plaintexts, then forge with the recovered relation.
Break a custom cipher given only its source and one ciphertext, recovering the plaintext - the same invert-the-scheme reasoning.
C++ brute force of a 16-bit residual keyspace validated by a known plaintext prefix, matched bit-exactly against an oracle binary.
C known-plaintext attack brute-forcing a 32-bit seed then decrypting the whole file to prove recovery, exactly FEAL's proof obligation.
C++ KPA recovering a 32-bit cipher state from a plaintext prefix and bulk-decrypting the remainder; same search-and-verify loop.
Solves algebraically for three cipher parameters from known plaintext instead of searching; the analytic half of a key-recovery attack.
Derives keystream bytes from a known header, then derives the cipher's unknown constants mathematically before decrypting.
Reads the cipher's Rust source and brute-forces a 16-bit seed; the reduced-seed hint in the FEAL prompt maps directly onto this.
XOR-seed cancellation in a rolling buzhash needs the same XOR/rotation algebra and S-box reasoning a Feistel linear approximation demands.

notes: TMax is by far the strongest pool: it has dozens of genuine known-plaintext / reduced-keyspace key-recovery tasks, so the final top 10 is 8/10 TMax. RTS is the weakest: its shortlist was almost entirely the 'encrypt Cybersecurity foundations. with AES-128-CBC and write a metadata report' boilerplate family (20+ near-duplicates, pure lexical false positives) - I dropped all of them and substituted crackme/symbolic-execution and Enigma tasks found by my own searches; ranks 9-10 there are weak and duplicative. TerminalWorld has exactly one strong candidate (tw_152765) and then falls off to password cracking with off-the-shelf tools. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have essentially no cryptanalysis; I judged them on bit-level/binary-algorithm skill and crypto-library domain, and their shortlists were driven entirely by the word 'key' (dict keys, key ordering, keyring) which I discarded.
